neighbours.label: whether an ongoing activity or term continues or ends: ceased, continue/continuing, terminated someone's appointment, long-term, end their lives
fire: The board terminated the director's contract after only two years.
The factory ceased operations in the spring of 1982.
The newspaper ceased publication after ninety years in print.
Adults in continuing education classes meet on Tuesday nights.
Workers with long-term back pain often miss days at the office.
After a vote, the council ended Mr Grant's tenure as chairman.
She plans to continue her research in Canada next year.
Old satellites eventually end their missions by burning up in the atmosphere.
quiet: The board approved the director's budget after only two meetings.
The factory opened a second canteen in the spring of 1982.
The newspaper won an award for its reporting on the floods.
Adults in pottery classes meet on Tuesday nights.
Workers with back pain are often advised to stretch at the office.
After a vote, the council praised Mr Grant as chairman.
She plans to present her research in Canada next year.
Old satellites are tracked by radar stations on the ground.

notes: Probe: 'terminated Nancy Knight's' 1.08 (peak 's), longer-term 0.77, ceased 0.71, continuing education 0.63, continue 0.39-0.42, 'end their' 0.40, stopped 0.23. Hired and 'was popular' were ≤0.08. Quiet items keep the same subject with a neutral event that neither continues nor stops.
